located_point.method: Not located in imagery. Coordinate printed for 'Ghadwadi (Khirsara)' in Bhan and Ajithprasad's Shikarpur 2007-2008 report (23 deg 27' 17.00" N, 69 deg 03' 35.99" E), within 1.2 km of the excavators' arcminute coordinate used by the site index. Renders at this point show fields, field hedges, a stream and the village to the west; no rectangle matching the fortified area of the plan could be outlined.

notes: Plan only, and the plan lines are a topographic proxy. The plan library had no Khirsara plan; the held article PDF has no site plan, so we downloaded its supplementary S1 Fig (CC BY). The figure's legend lists only contour lines and modern structures: the fortification of the 'Gadh Wali Wadi', which the article text calls a fortified settlement, appears only as straight bundles of contour lines along a rampart mound. We picked the centre of each straight bundle at both ends by hand with a 1-sigma uncertainty of 8 pixels (about 1.8 m). The west and south sides (theta -10.1 and -8.6) form the main system; the east side (theta -1.2) differs by more than 6 degrees and stands alone. The enclosure drawn by the contours is therefore not rectangular. These values describe the rampart mound's line and should be compared with wall measurements with that in mind.
